evidence.note: Mirrors jev-lint's validated built-ins ts-test-cannot-fail / swift-test-cannot-fail: holdout 12/12 per language, 0 false positives. Evidence that the wording works, not new evidence for this language.

Banik et al. (preprint, Jun 2026), 86,156 agent-authored test-file patches (Codex, Copilot, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code): 80.2% weak/no oracle; W1 no-assertion 24-85% by agent; W2 existence-only 0-0.4%; W4 mock-only 0-4%; W5 snapshot-only 0-4%.
Hora & Robbes, MSR 2026: 1.2M commits/2,168 TS/JS/Python repos; 23% of agent commits touch tests vs 13% human; 36% of agent commits add mocks vs 26% human.

rs-test-cannot-fail.whyNotLinter: Clippy has no lint requiring a behaviour-dependent assertion in tests.
rs-test-cannot-fail.aiRelevance: Banik et al. find 80.2% of agent-authored test-file patches carry weak or no oracle signals (no-assertion is the largest class); Hora & Robbes find agents add mocks in 36% of commits vs 26% for humans.
rs-test-cannot-fail.expectedNoise: low-med — Rust tests often rely on unwrap-as-assertion; the false list spells out when that counts.
rs-test-cannot-fail.notes: Refines best-practices/rust.md rs-test-cannot-fail: gate now covers rstest/test_case/proptest and any `path::test` attribute.
